chapter.li: Verse30 Now the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus and told him all things, both what they had done and what they had taught. VerseEnd Verse31 And he said unto them, You, come yourselves, apart into a solitary place, and rest awhile; for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure, not so much as to eat. VerseEnd

Verse32 And they departed into a solitary place by ship, privately, VerseEnd Verse33 and the people saw them departing; and many knew Jesus, and ran on foot there out of all cities, and outran them, and came together unto him. VerseEnd Verse34 And Jesus, when he came out, saw many people and was moved with compassion towards them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things. VerseEnd

Verse35 And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him and said, This is a solitary place, and now the time for departure has come. VerseEnd Verse36 Send them away, that they may go into the country round about and into the villages, and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat. VerseEnd Verse37 And he answered and said unto them, You give them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennies worth of bread and give them to eat? VerseEnd Verse38 He said unto them, How many loaves do you have? Go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes. VerseEnd Verse39 And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass. VerseEnd

Verse40 And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties. VerseEnd Verse41 And when he had taken the five loaves and two fishes, he looked up to Heaven and blessed and broke the loaves, and gave to his disciples to set before the multitude. And the two fishes divided he among them all. VerseEnd Verse42 And they did all eat and were filled. VerseEnd Verse43 And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments and of the fishes. VerseEnd Verse44 And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men. VerseEnd

Verse45 And immediately he constrained his disciples to get into the ship and to go to the other side before him, unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people. VerseEnd Verse46 And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray. VerseEnd

Verse47 And when evening had come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land; VerseEnd Verse48 and he saw them toiling in rowing, for the wind was contrary unto them. And about the fourth watch of the night, he comes unto them, walking upon the sea, as if he would have passed by them. VerseEnd Verse49 And when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit and cried out, VerseEnd Verse50 for they all saw him and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them and said unto them, Be of good cheer, it is I. Be not afraid. VerseEnd Verse51 And he went up unto them, into the ship, and the wind ceased. And they were utterly amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered VerseEnd — Verse52 for they considered not of the loaves, for their hearts were hardened. VerseEnd

Verse53 And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret and drew to the shore. VerseEnd Verse54 And when they had come out of the ship, immediately the people knew him VerseEnd Verse55 and ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was. VerseEnd Verse56 And wherever he entered, into villages or cities or country, they laid the sick in the streets and implored him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garments. And as many as touched him were made whole. VerseEnd

LEChapter7 Verse1 Then came together unto him the Pharisees and certain of the scribes, who came from Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse2 And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled (that is to say, with unwashed) hands, they found fault; VerseEnd Verse3 for the Pharisees and all the Jews, except they wash hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders. VerseEnd Verse4 And when they come from the market, except they wash their bodies, they eat not. And many other things there are which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups and pots, brazen vessels, and of dining couches. VerseEnd Verse5 And the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why do your disciples not walk according to the traditions of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands? VerseEnd

Verse6 He answered and said unto them, Well has Isaiah prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; VerseEnd Verse7 nevertheless, in vain do they worship me, teaching the doctrines and commandments of men. VerseEnd Verse8 For laying aside the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men — the washing of pots and of cups, and many other such like things you do. VerseEnd Verse9 And he said unto them, Yea, altogether you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your own traditions. Full well is it written of you by the prophets whom you have rejected. They testified these things truly and their blood shall be upon you.

You have kept not the ordinances of God; VerseEnd Verse10 for Moses said, Honor your father and your mother, and whoever curses father or mother, let him die the death VerseEnd Verse11 of the transgressor, as it is written in your law. But you keep not the law. You say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, Corban (that is to say, a gift by whatsoever you might be profited by me), he is of age, VerseEnd Verse12 and you suffer him no more to do anything for his father or his mother, VerseEnd Verse13 making the word of God of no effect through your tradition which you have delivered. And many such things do you. VerseEnd

Verse14 And when he had called all the people, he said unto them, Listen unto me, everyone, and understand. VerseEnd Verse15 There is nothing from outside that, entering into a man, can defile him (which is food). But the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man; that proceeds forth out of the heart. VerseEnd Verse16 If any man has ears to hear, let him hear. VerseEnd

Verse17 And when he had entered into the house from among the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable. VerseEnd Verse18 And he said unto them, Are you without understanding also? Do you not perceive that whatever thing from outside enters into the man cannot defile him? VerseEnd Verse19 Because it enters not into his heart but into the belly, and goes out into the waste, purging all foods. VerseEnd Verse20 And he said, That which comes out of the man defiles the man; VerseEnd Verse21 for from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, VerseEnd Verse22 thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. VerseEnd Verse23 All these evil things come from within and defile the man. VerseEnd

Verse24 And from there he arose and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into a house, and desired that no man should come unto him. But he could not deny them, for he had compassion upon all men. VerseEnd Verse25 For a woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet. VerseEnd Verse26 The woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by nation. And she implored him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter. VerseEnd Verse27 But Jesus said unto her, Let the children of the kingdom first be filled, for it is not meet to take the children’s bread and to cast it unto the dogs. VerseEnd Verse28 And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord, you say truly; yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs. VerseEnd Verse29 And he said unto her, For this saying, go your way; the devil is gone out of your daughter. VerseEnd Verse30 And when she had come to her house, she found that the devil had gone out and her daughter was laid upon the bed. VerseEnd

Verse31 And again departing from the regions of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of Decapolis. VerseEnd Verse32 And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech. And they implored him to put his hand upon him. VerseEnd Verse33 And he took him aside from the multitude and put his finger into his ears, and he spit and touched his tongue. VerseEnd Verse34 And, looking up to Heaven, he sighed and said unto him, Ephphatha (that is, Be opened) VerseEnd. Verse35 And immediately his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was untied and he spoke plain. VerseEnd Verse36 And he charged them that they should tell no man. But the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published him, VerseEnd Verse37 and were beyond measure astonished, saying, He has done all things well. He makes both the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak. VerseEnd

LEChapter8 Verse1 In those days, the multitude being very great and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples and said unto them, VerseEnd Verse2 I have compassion on the multitude because they have now been with me three days and have nothing to eat. VerseEnd Verse3 And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way, for some of them came from afar. VerseEnd Verse4 And his disciples answered him, From where can a man satisfy these, so great a multitude, with bread here in the wilderness? VerseEnd Verse5 And he asked them, How many loaves do you have? And they said, Seven. VerseEnd Verse6 And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground.

And he took the seven loaves and gave thanks, and broke and gave to his disciples to set before the people. And they did set them before the people. VerseEnd Verse7 And they had a few small fishes, and he blessed them and commanded to set them also before the people, that they should eat. VerseEnd Verse8 So they did eat and were filled. And they took up of the broken bread that was left seven baskets. VerseEnd Verse9 And they that had eaten were about four thousand. And he sent them away. VerseEnd

Verse10 And directly he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the ports of Dalmanutha. VerseEnd Verse11 And the Pharisees came forth and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from Heaven, testing him. VerseEnd Verse12 And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and said, Why does this generation seek after a sign? Truly I say unto you, there shall be no sign given unto this generation save the sign of the prophet Jonah; for as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly, so likewise shall the Son of Man be buried in the bowels of the earth. VerseEnd Verse13 And he left them, and, entering into the ship again, he departed to the other side. VerseEnd

Verse14 Now the multitude had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf. VerseEnd Verse15 And he charged them, saying, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod. VerseEnd Verse16 And they reasoned among themselves, saying, He has said this because we have no bread. VerseEnd

Verse17 And when they said this among themselves, Jesus knew it. And he said unto them, Why do you reason because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive? Neither understand? Are your hearts yet hardened? VerseEnd Verse18 Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember VerseEnd Verse19 when I broke the five loaves among the five thousand? How many baskets full of fragments did you take up? They say unto him, Twelve. VerseEnd Verse20 And when the seven among the four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up? And they said, Seven. VerseEnd Verse21 And he said unto them, How is it that you do not understand? VerseEnd

Verse22 And he comes to Bethsaida. And they bring a blind man unto him and implored him to touch him. VerseEnd Verse23 And he took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the town. And when he had spit upon his eyes and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw anything. VerseEnd Verse24 And he looked up and he said, I see men as trees walking. VerseEnd Verse25 After that, he put his hands again upon his eyes and made him look up, and he was restored and saw every man clearly. VerseEnd Verse26 And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town nor tell what is done to any in the town. VerseEnd
